non_goals: No enterprise GPU cluster orchestration (multi-node Kubernetes/Slurm farms or commercial MLOps stacks).

No custom benchmarking or smoke-test frameworks (rely on primary evaluations and 1-line upstream built-in sanity checks).
No mirroring upstream installation manuals (own curated paths, cross-tool glue, real-world traps, and canonical upstream deep-links).
No museum of legacy options (one active anchor per Workflow Slot; superseded picks move cleanly to Retired and Superseded ADR history).

google-ai-studio.name: Google AI Studio (Gemini 4 Hydrogen & 3.8 Flash)
google-ai-studio.summary: Google's primary card-free developer API gateway serving Gemini 4 Hydrogen with a 1,048,576-token unified context window, multimodal inputs, and four thinking levels alongside Gemini Decision 1.
google-ai-studio.when_to_use: Default zero-card cloud gateway for multi-step coding agents, full-repository ingestion, and multimodal reasoning.
limitations: Free Tier prompts are used to improve products outside EU/UK/CH; never paste secrets or proprietary source code.
Search Grounding, Maps Grounding, Batch API, and explicit context caching are paid-tier only on Gemini 4 Hydrogen.
Passing thinking_level=minimal or out-of-range temperature/top_p/top_k returns HTTP 400 on gemini-4-hydrogen.

meta.quota: No card: Free Tier (gemini-4-hydrogen 1M unified ctx, implicit caching) + Decision 1 (200 RPM / 10K RPD)

zhipu-bigmodel.name: Z.ai BigModel (GLM-4.7-Flash)
zhipu-bigmodel.summary: Card-free developer API offering a permanently free MIT-licensed GLM-4.7-Flash endpoint with a 200K context window and 128K output cap.
zhipu-bigmodel.when_to_use: Secondary card-free backup for long-context coding and tool-use loops when Google AI Studio limits are hit.
limitations: Only glm-4.7-flash is permanently free; newer GLM-5.x endpoints are billed and fail on $0 accounts.

meta.quota: No card: permanently free GLM-4.7-Flash tier (200K ctx / 128K out)

nvidia-nim.name: NVIDIA NIM Developer Catalog
nvidia-nim.summary: Serverless developer catalog hosting rack-scale open-weight checkpoints—including 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL—without requiring a credit card.
nvidia-nim.when_to_use: Prototyping giant 300B-550B open-weight models that exceed consumer workstation memory.
limitations: Restricted to developer prototyping rather than production workloads, with occasional cold-start queues on large MoEs.

meta.quota: No card: ~40 RPM developer prototyping catalog (keys generated at build.nvidia.com)

openrouter-free.name: OpenRouter (:free Routes)
openrouter-free.summary: Unified OpenAI-compatible aggregator routing community-sponsored free model endpoints behind one API key.
openrouter-free.when_to_use: Quick side-by-side model comparisons and light fallback routing across diverse open weights.
limitations: 50 RPD on unverified $0 accounts runs out in roughly three multi-step coding tasks; negative balances return HTTP 402 even on :free routes.

meta.quota: 20 RPM, 50 RPD ($0 balance) -> 1,000 RPD (>=10 credits balance)

groq-cloud.name: Groq Cloud LPU
groq-cloud.summary: Ultra-low-latency LPU inference offering free tiers for compact LLMs (qwen/qwen3.8-27b) and high-quota Whisper-Large-v3 speech transcription.
groq-cloud.when_to_use: Sub-second small-prompt JSON routing (<6K tokens) and free audio transcription (2,000 requests/day).
limitations: Strict 8,000 TPM cap on free LLMs causes immediate HTTP 429 failures on 20K-token coding agent prompts.

meta.quota: No card: LLMs 30 RPM / 1K RPD / 8K TPM; Whisper 2K RPD / 28.8K audio sec/day

cloudflare-workers-ai.name: Cloudflare Workers AI (Clef & Clairic)
cloudflare-workers-ai.summary: Edge inference offering 10,000 daily free Neurons for non-autoregressive Clef decision models and Clairic structured span extraction.
cloudflare-workers-ai.when_to_use: Zero-output-token edge classification, moderation, and typed extraction.
limitations: Legacy Workers AI generative catalog models were hard-retired on Nov 20, 2026 (HTTP 410).

pollinations.name: Pollinations AI
pollinations.summary: Keyless community OpenAI-compatible text and FLUX image endpoint requiring zero signup or authentication.
pollinations.when_to_use: Last-resort keyless fallback for throwaway public sandbox tests where no API keys exist.
limitations: Shared public community service; never transmit private code, credentials, or personal data.

meta.quota: Keyless fair-use IP quota (text and image)

firecrawl.name: Firecrawl
firecrawl.summary: JavaScript-capable webpage-to-Markdown crawler with an agent onboarding skill and low token overhead on OpenBenchmarks.
firecrawl.when_to_use: Turning modern dynamic documentation sites into clean Markdown for research and RAG.
limitations: Keyless usage is strictly IP-rate-limited; create a free API key for multi-page crawls.

jina-reader.name: Jina Reader (r.jina.ai / s.jina.ai)
jina-reader.summary: Zero-SDK URL prefix service turning web pages and PDFs into clean LLM-ready Markdown.
jina-reader.when_to_use: One-line URL reading inside shell scripts and lightweight agents.
limitations: Unauthenticated prefix requests throttle quickly under automated batch loops.

meta.quota: Keyless prefix + 10M free tokens with free API key

exa-search.name: Exa 3.0 Neural Search
exa-search.summary: Semantic web search API built specifically for AI retrieval, renewing $10/month in free credits on the 1st of every month.
exa-search.when_to_use: High-precision web discovery for research agents and technical literature scouting.
limitations: Deep search modes exhaust monthly free credits much faster than Lite searches.

meta.quota: No card: $10/mo recurring credits (~2,500 Lite searches)

openalex.name: OpenAlex Academic Graph
openalex.summary: Open scholarly index covering 250M+ academic works, citation graphs, and open-access PDF links with zero API keys required.
openalex.when_to_use: Primary literature review, DOI verification, and academic citation mapping.
limitations: Pass ?mailto=you@domain.com in queries to enter the fast polite pool.

gpt-researcher.name: GPT Researcher
gpt-researcher.summary: Open-source research synthesizer (MCP + skill) covering both live web sources and local PDF/CSV folders.
gpt-researcher.when_to_use: Generating structured, cited background reports over mixed web and local documents.
limitations: Audit every cited claim, date, and quantitative metric against primary sources before publishing.

deerflow.name: DeerFlow 2.0
deerflow.summary: Open-source deep research harness executing web gathering, code analysis, and synthesis inside an isolated Docker sandbox.
deerflow.when_to_use: Multi-step deep research reports when you want container-isolated execution.
limitations: Requires Docker and careful prompt/token budgeting to avoid runaway web fetches.

tailscale-serve.name: Tailscale Serve (Loopback-to-Tailnet HTTPS Mesh)
tailscale-serve.summary: Zero-port WireGuard overlay exposing 127.0.0.1-bound local servers (llama-server, mlx_lm.server, ComfyUI, pi-mobile) privately inside your tailnet with automatic HTTPS and ACL tags.
tailscale-serve.when_to_use: Developer standard for connecting Mac mini, NVIDIA GPU PC, and Android/iOS phones without opening router ports.
limitations: Automatic Let's Encrypt HTTPS certificates log machine.<tailnet>.ts.net hostnames in public CT logs; use neutral box names (e.g., box-a).

lm-link.name: LM Link (Tailscale tsnet Zero-VPN GPU Sharing)
lm-link.summary: Userspace Tailscale mesh built into LM Studio and headless llmster (lms link enable) that projects a remote home GPU onto localhost:1234 on your travel laptop with zero OS VPN setup.
lm-link.when_to_use: Newcomers and students wanting to borrow their home desktop GPU from a thin laptop without configuring Tailscale ACLs.
limitations: Free during Preview; paid tiers are planned at General Availability (use Tailscale Serve for permanent open control).

pi-mobile-voice.name: pi-mobile (Multi-Box Tailscale HTTPS & Voice Mode)
pi-mobile-voice.summary: E2E-encrypted Pi package uniting multiple computers (/remote add box) into one phone queue sorted by 'who needs you', answering any extension dialog with Voice Mode and 2-min desk-idle mute.
pi-mobile-voice.when_to_use: Live hands-free HITL steering across a Mac mini, GPU PC, and cloud VM with spoken behavioral summaries and verbal confirmation.
limitations: A paired phone equals shell access on your home machine; keep behind Tailscale ACLs and neutral hostnames.

pi-mobile-android.name: ayagmar/pi-mobile (Native Android Compose Client)
pi-mobile-android.summary: Open-source Jetpack Compose Android client bridging to Pi RPC over Tailscale (*.ts.net) with terminal QR pairing, live /tree branch navigation/forking, image uploads, and bash dialog.
pi-mobile-android.when_to_use: Android developers wanting a dedicated native client with full /tree session branching on macOS or Linux hosts.
limitations: Requires Tailscale active on both host and Android device plus the Node RPC bridge daemon.

pi-durable-telegram.name: smixs/pi-durable-telegram (Durable Async Telegram Bot)
pi-durable-telegram.summary: SQLite-backed Telegram HITL bridge built directly on @earendil-works/pi-durable using outbound long-polling (zero open ports) with photo, PDF, voice note, and file delivery.
pi-durable-telegram.when_to_use: Zero-extra-app async HITL communication, multimodal mobile capture, and crash-resumable remote jobs.
limitations: One-command installer configures a Linux systemd user service; run manually or via launchd on macOS, and never run two pollers on one bot token.

opencode-mobile.name: dzianisv/opencode-mobile (Android HITL Client)
opencode-mobile.summary: Open-source Android client (F-Droid/APK) connecting to opencode serve over Tailscale/LAN with native tool-call approval dialogs and Android Keystore authentication.
opencode-mobile.when_to_use: Mobile approval and monitoring for OpenCode sessions without switching harnesses.
limitations: Always configure OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD and route over Tailscale rather than unencrypted LAN.

ntfy-push.name: ntfy (One-Way HOOTL Awareness Pings)
ntfy-push.summary: Simple HTTP pub-sub push notification server (self-hostable or free 250 msgs/day on ntfy.sh) with up to 3 actionable HTTP buttons.
ntfy-push.when_to_use: Notifying your phone the moment an unattended build, ComfyUI render, or nightly audit completes or stalls.
limitations: One-way notification channel; pair with Telegram or pi-mobile when you need interactive multi-turn steering.

google-antigravity.name: Google Antigravity ($0 Individual Tier)
google-antigravity.summary: Zero-install agentic coding suite spanning native desktop App, IDE extensions, and agy CLI with unlimited Tab/Command completions and weekly free agent quota.
google-antigravity.when_to_use: Fastest 5-minute guided entry into agentic coding for newcomers and students on any laptop.
limitations: Free agent quota resets weekly with no rollover; managed Google Workspace or .edu accounts may hit entitlement walls (use a personal Google account).
No official first-party mobile companion app as of Nov 2026.

meta.quota: $0/mo Individual: unlimited Tab & Command + weekly Work-Done agent quota

opencode.name: OpenCode CLI & Desktop
opencode.summary: Mature, vendor-agnostic coding harness with 1-line install, built-in per-action approval prompts, offline share-disabled mode, and an official HF Qwen3.8-27B adapter.
opencode.when_to_use: Default local coding harness for newcomers and teams wanting safe out-of-the-box permission prompts.
limitations: Place baseURL strictly inside options, name the file opencode.json (no leading dot), and never name your custom provider 'openai'.
opencode serve starts without a password by default; set OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD before exposing beyond 127.0.0.1.

meta.config_title: Working opencode.json for local llama-server (avoids the 4 beginner traps)
meta.sanity_check: opencode debug config && opencode models local

pi.name: Pi Coding Agent (+ @earendil-works/pi-durable)
pi.summary: Minimal, hackable agent kernel with built-in /llama router support, /v1/systemone decision-model discovery, /tree DAG branching, MCP + Codemode JS sandbox, and SQLite durability.
pi.when_to_use: Flagship developer anchor: run naked in 5 minutes, or optionally rice across 6 modular rungs (LoRA, sandbox, smart MCP, durability, mobile HITL, ComfyUI).
limitations: Intentionally omits built-in per-tool approval prompts; pair with gondolin, nono, or safeagents before autonomous runs.
Requires Node 22.19+; built-in MCP keeps enabled servers alive all session unless replaced with pi-mcp-adapter.

deepseek-harness.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
deepseek-harness.summary: Cordis plugin-everything agent platform where even the core agent loop is a swappable plugin, shipping a read-only-by-default sandbox and sub-agent plugins.
deepseek-harness.when_to_use: Experimenting with custom loop architectures, Creator Mode live UI plugins, or web/desktop sessions.
limitations: Rapidly iterating developer preview; pin plugin peer versions against breaking interface changes.

hermes-agent.name: Hermes Agent
hermes-agent.summary: Persistent self-improving daemon featuring cross-session memory, autonomous skill authoring, cron scheduling, native Telegram/WhatsApp bridges, and HF adapter support.
hermes-agent.when_to_use: Always-on background ops daemons and scheduled digests where you want messaging built in from day one.
limitations: Foreground sessions do not auto-compact aggressively like Pi by default (though idle gateway chats now background-compact in v0.23.5); cap context lengths on massive repositories.

llama-cpp.name: llama.cpp (Mainline GGUF Server & Router)
llama-cpp.summary: Universal CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, and ROCm serving engine supporting hybrid MoE offloading (--n-cpu-moe), runtime --lora loading, router mode (llama serve), and Inkling looped layers (#32218).
llama-cpp.when_to_use: Primary local serving engine on NVIDIA workstations and built-in /llama backend for Pi.
limitations: --sleep-idle-seconds leaves ~600 MiB of dormant CUDA context VRAM attached per model (llama.cpp#19379); explicitly Unload via Pi /llama before heavy ComfyUI renders.
--no-mmap is deprecated; use --load-mode none instead.

mlx-lm.name: Apple MLX (mlx-lm)
mlx-lm.summary: Apple Silicon native unified-memory inference framework beating llama.cpp by 46% to 3x on Apple GPUs with ~65 tok/s on 4-bit Qwen3.8-27B builds.
mlx-lm.when_to_use: Primary local LLM serving engine on Apple Silicon Macs (Mac mini, MacBook Pro, Mac Studio).
limitations: Prompt prefill lags dedicated NVIDIA Tensor Cores; 32GB+ unified memory is recommended for 27B coding sessions.

unsloth-runtime.name: Unsloth Runtime & Studio
unsloth-runtime.summary: Optimized local runtime offering fast VRAM-exceeding MoE execution, Decision API hosting for Laya, Anthropic-compatible local endpoints, and lower-memory 4-bit LoRA training.
unsloth-runtime.when_to_use: Serving Dynamic v3.1 GGUFs, local Laya decision endpoints, or running local LoRA fine-tunes.
limitations: Keep Studio updated alongside mainline llama.cpp when adopting newly released quantization formats.

wangp.name: WanGP v20.21 (One-Stop Low-VRAM Media Studio)
wangp.summary: Guided-installer local studio covering Video (Wan 2.2, H3), Images (Qwen-Image-2.1, FLUX.2), Music, Speech, and 3D inside one browser UI starting at 6 GB VRAM, plus native MCP.
wangp.when_to_use: Default turnkey local media setup for newcomers and 6GB-16GB NVIDIA workstations (5.9-14.3 GiB video VRAM vs ComfyUI's 22.7-23.5 GiB).
limitations: Install WGPKernels 1.5.0 and SageGP 1.0.2 (PyTorch 2.10; Triton 3.6+ required for RTX 50-series adaptive Sage2/3).
Heavy local video synthesis targets NVIDIA GPUs; Mac users should route heavy video to a remote GPU PC or Comfy Cloud.
GitHub /releases/latest tracks WanGP Manager (manager-v0.1.21) while core studio wgp.py ships on main at v20.21.

meta.footprint: 6-15 GB NVIDIA VRAM (MMGP v4 + Extreme Chunker)

comfyui.name: ComfyUI (Comfy-Org Programmable Node Graph)
comfyui.summary: Canonical node-graph media engine (v0.46+) supporting custom multi-stage workflows, RAFT Video Deflicker, Bria RMBG 3.0, and first-party agent automation via MCP.
comfyui.when_to_use: Developers building reproducible multi-stage media graphs or driving local/remote GPU rendering from Pi.
limitations: Official ComfyUI docs explicitly advise Mac users away from heavy local video on Apple MPS (FP8 crashes MPS); target a remote NVIDIA box or Comfy Cloud.
For Qwen-Image-2.1 on 16GB NVIDIA cards, use Comfy-Org INT8 or leejet/ComfyUI-GGUF (city96/ComfyUI-GGUF throws unknown architecture).

meta.footprint: 8-24 GB NVIDIA VRAM (use Comfy-Org INT8 or leejet/ComfyUI-GGUF on 16GB)

comfy-mcp.name: Comfy-Org Official comfy-mcp (Local & Cloud)
comfy-mcp.summary: First-party open-source local MCP server (pip install comfy-mcp, zero account) and hosted Comfy Cloud MCP supporting remote Tailscale GPU hosts via COMFYUI_URL with inline media previews.
comfy-mcp.when_to_use: Default agent-to-ComfyUI bridge for Pi, OpenCode, and Antigravity across local, Tailscale, or Comfy Cloud backends.
limitations: Local launch/restart requires comfy-cli >= 1.14.0 (>= 1.16.0 for job watching), and v0.11.0 skips local launch/restart whenever COMFYUI_URL is set for remote Tailscale hosts.
On a single 16GB GPU, explicitly unload the local LLM in Pi (/llama) before queuing heavy ComfyUI video workflows.

comfyui-mcp.name: artokun/comfyui-mcp (Power-User Control Plane)
comfyui-mcp.summary: Feature-rich community ComfyUI MCP server adding bundled model-family skills, a /system_stats VRAM watchdog (<1 GB warning), explicit VRAM freeing, and autonomous workflow debugging.
comfyui-mcp.when_to_use: Power users wanting automated workflow debugging, Mermaid graph conversion, and active VRAM management on 16GB rigs.
limitations: Community-maintained; verify compatibility alongside Comfy-Org's first-party comfy-mcp updates.

wan-2.2.name: Wan 2.2 (5B & A14B Apache-2.0 Video)
wan-2.2.summary: Permissive Apache-2.0 open-weight video synthesis model running smoothly inside 6-15 GB VRAM via WanGP.
wan-2.2.when_to_use: Commercial-safe local video generation on consumer NVIDIA GPUs.
limitations: Newer Wan 3.0 and Wan 2.6 releases remain closed cloud APIs with no published local weights.

meta.footprint: 6-15 GB VRAM via WanGP MMGP v4

qwen-image-2.1.name: Qwen-Image-2.1 (7B DiT Native RGBA)
qwen-image-2.1.summary: Compact 7B diffusion transformer supporting native transparent RGBA output and clean 2048px typography inside 16GB VRAM.
qwen-image-2.1.when_to_use: Non-commercial design assets, typography, and layered transparent image editing.
limitations: Non-commercial license; swap to Apache-2.0 FLUX.2 Klein for commercial production graphics.

hyperframes.name: HeyGen Hyperframes
hyperframes.summary: Programmatic HTML-to-MP4 studio producing crisp deterministic UI demos, explainers, and launch motion graphics.
hyperframes.when_to_use: Code-driven product demos and technical videos where diffusion flicker is undesirable.
limitations: Designed for structured UI/data motion graphics rather than photorealistic live-action video.

phonon-31m.name: Gradium Phonon 31M WebGPU TTS
phonon-31m.summary: 64.5 MB Apache-2.0 English voice synthesis running directly inside any WebGPU browser at 4.9ms first-audio latency with zero CUDA setup.
phonon-31m.when_to_use: Instant zero-install local speech synthesis for students, Mac users, and browser workflows.
limitations: Compact English voice model; heavier multilingual dramatic acting requires larger server-side TTS models.

playwright-mcp.name: Microsoft Playwright MCP
playwright-mcp.summary: Official browser accessibility-tree automation server supporting Planner, Generator, and Healer end-to-end QA agents.
playwright-mcp.when_to_use: Verifying web applications, forms, and visual regressions directly from Pi, OpenCode, or Antigravity.
limitations: Accessibility snapshots cannot inspect inside closed Shadow DOM.

context7.name: Upstash Context7 (ctx7 & @upstash/context7-pi)
context7.summary: Injects live, version-matched library documentation directly into coding agents, eliminating stale training-cutoff API hallucinations.
context7.when_to_use: Working with fast-moving web, Python, or mobile SDKs.
limitations: Pin local Context7 servers to >= 2.1.3 (CVE-2026-75130) and explicitly instruct agents in AGENTS.md to call it.

mobile-build-mcp.name: Sentry MobileBuildMCP
mobile-build-mcp.summary: Builds Apple iOS/macOS targets, runs XCTest suites, and attaches LLDB directly from coding agents (formerly XcodeBuildMCP).
mobile-build-mcp.when_to_use: Native Apple Swift/iOS/macOS development on Apple Silicon Macs.
limitations: Stops at Apple builds and simulators; physical USB Android/iOS UI testing requires separate device tooling.

obra-superpowers.name: obra/superpowers (15-Skill Engineering Pack)
obra-superpowers.summary: High-leverage SKILL.md pack enforcing Brainstorm -> Spec -> Red/Green TDD -> Fresh Subagent -> Verification before claiming completion.
obra-superpowers.when_to_use: Eliminating agent drift during multi-hour autonomous coding sessions across Pi, OpenCode, Antigravity, and Hermes.
limitations: On Hermes Agent, use the Hermes-native tool mapping port rather than raw Claude Code tool names.

pi-mcp-adapter.name: nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter (Lazy & Semantic MCP)
pi-mcp-adapter.summary: Drop-in Pi MCP replacement adding lazy server startup, 10-minute idle shutdown, OS keychain OAuth, and semantic tool ranking via Jev/Clef (10/11 vs 5/11 across 95 tools).
pi-mcp-adapter.when_to_use: Rung 3 of the Pi Ricing Journey once you attach more than 3-4 MCP servers and want zero context bloat.
limitations: Automatically replaces Pi's built-in MCP handler upon installation.

obsidian-skills.name: Obsidian Official Agent Skills (1.2.3 + defuddle + obsidian-headless)
obsidian-skills.summary: Official Obsidian skill pack working across Antigravity, Hermes, OpenCode, and Pi, bundling Markdown/Bases/Canvas rules, headless CLI sync, and kepano/defuddle web clipping.
obsidian-skills.when_to_use: Building a human-readable, Git/Obsidian-friendly personal knowledge vault that both you and your agents maintain.
limitations: Treat all web pages clipped through defuddle strictly as untrusted data, never as executable agent instructions.

qmd-search.name: tobi/qmd (Local BM25 + Vector Markdown Search & MCP)
qmd-search.summary: 100% local hybrid search CLI and MCP server combining BM25 keyword precision, local embeddings, and reranking directly over plain Markdown folders.
qmd-search.when_to_use: Searching large local Obsidian/Git knowledge vaults privately with zero cloud vector databases.
limitations: Keep qmd vector index files machine-local; exclude them from Git/Syncthing/Obsidian Sync to avoid corruption.

pi-obsidian-memory.name: pi-obsidian-memory (KV-Cache-Stable Vault Memory for Pi)
pi-obsidian-memory.summary: MIT Pi extensions connecting plain-Markdown Obsidian vaults with deterministic /rule, /memory, and daily logs (the-matt-moo) or Jev/Laya relevance scoring (davy121) inside a bounded char budget.
pi-obsidian-memory.when_to_use: Giving Pi persistent cross-session memory without invalidating local llama.cpp/MLX KV prefix caches every turn.
limitations: Keep ambient memory as a session-stable snapshot (refreshing only on deliberate writes) so local KV prefix caches do not thrash.

qwen3.8-27b.name: Qwen3.8-27B (Dense Vision + Text)
qwen3.8-27b.summary: Apache-2.0 27B dense model serving as the primary 16GB VRAM and Apple Silicon coding backbone, hosting both Hugging Face's RL harness adapters and compact uncensored LoRAs on one frozen file.
qwen3.8-27b.when_to_use: Daily-driver local coding, strict instruction following, and single-backbone multi-LoRA serving.
limitations: On 16GB GPUs, keep quantization at IQ4_XS with Q8 KV cache so weights never spill over PCIe.
Avoid Ollama's /v1/chat/completions endpoint with qwen3.8:27b due to reported hangs; use llama-server or mlx_lm.server.
Not suited for 8GB-12GB student laptops; use $0 Cloud or Gemma 4 12B on smaller hardware.

qwen3-coder-next.name: Qwen3-Coder-Next (80B-A3B Sparse MoE)
qwen3-coder-next.summary: Sparse 512-expert Mixture-of-Experts coding model activating only 3B parameters per token, making 80B-class capacity practical in 16GB VRAM + 64GB DDR5 hybrid mode.
qwen3-coder-next.when_to_use: Deeper multi-file repository reasoning on 16GB GPU + 64GB RAM workstations or 64GB+ Macs.
limitations: Keep -ngl 99 so Attention and KV cache stay in GPU VRAM; offload cold experts only via --n-cpu-moe.

meta.launch_recipe: GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_OPT=1 llama-server -m Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ngl 99 -fa on -c 120000 --load-mode none --n-cpu-moe 29 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --temp 0

gemma-4.name: Gemma 4 Family (12B Tri-Modal & 26B-A4B Vision)
gemma-4.summary: Fast Apache-2.0 open-weight family providing a clean 8.5 GB laptop/student off-ramp (12B with native audio) and ~140 tok/s text+vision throughput on 16GB VRAM (26B-A4B).
gemma-4.when_to_use: 8GB-12GB laptops needing local chat/audio, or ultra-fast 16GB vision and general chat.
limitations: Only E2B, E4B, and 12B process audio; the 26B-A4B MoE checkpoint is Text + Vision only.

hermes-4.name: NousResearch Hermes 4 (14B / 4.3-36B Neutral)
hermes-4.summary: Neutral-aligned open-weight checkpoints designed to follow operator-defined system prompt policies cleanly without weight-surgery degradation.
hermes-4.when_to_use: Self-hosted deployments needing predictable operator-controlled behavior rather than abliteration.
limitations: Always author explicit safety policies in your system prompt if exposing the endpoint beyond solo local use.

inkling-2-mini.name: Inkling 2 Mini (26.4B Looped Transformer MoE)
inkling-2-mini.summary: Experimental looped-layer MoE iterating its middle 12 layers three times (3.4B base / 5.4B effective active, 1M context), natively supported in mainline llama.cpp (#32218) and Unsloth.
inkling-2-mini.when_to_use: Testing high-efficiency looped coding architectures inside 16GB-18GB memory budgets.

frontier.name: Claude Fable 5.2 & Mythos 5.2
frontier.summary: Sets the current ceiling for 10-12 hour autonomous audits (1M ctx / 128K out, 89.3% OSWorld 2.1, 69.9% FrontierSWE v2), with Mythos 5.2 focused on security and Lean proofs.

frontier.name: GPT-6.2 Astra & GPT-6.2 Sol
frontier.summary: Introduces cache-preserving mid-conversation reasoning-effort and tool toggling—an API caching pattern worth watching for future local vLLM and llama.cpp harnesses.
limitations: Paid API only; monitor-only.

frontier.name: Gemini 4 Carbon & 4 Argon
frontier.summary: Leads autonomous workflow execution (53.9% AutomationBench) powering Spark Task mode; its fast sibling Gemini 4 Hydrogen has already trickled down into the Free Tier.
limitations: Paid Pro/Ultra and billed API only.

frontier.name: Qwen4-Max (2.4T)
frontier.summary: 2.4T frontier release (1M ctx, 262K CoT); Alibaba confirmed smaller open-weight Qwen4 releases are planned next, making this the primary reversal-trigger signal for Qwen3.8-27B.
limitations: Current 2.4T checkpoint is cloud API only; await smaller open-weight checkpoints.

frontier.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (552B)
frontier.summary: Asymmetric Causal Encoder-Decoder (8B active in / 16B out) achieving a 1/4 HBM KV cache footprint; watch for smaller open weights adopting this KV compression.
limitations: Exceeds 16GB VRAM + 64GB RAM local memory; accessible via NVIDIA NIM prototyping API.

community.name: disler/durable-pi Multi-Device Agent Showcase

community.name: Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-Nomas Walkable Worlds
community.summary: Single-GPU WASD-navigable world generator chained by indie creators with LTX-2.5 for video-conditioned audio prototyping.

community.name: shaftoe/awesome-pi-coding-agent (CI-Updated Extension Index)

limitations: Explicitly prototype-grade; tracked to monitor emerging mobile HITL credential-gating patterns.
